therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: NK1 receptor antagonism, 5-HT3 receptor antagonism, glucocorticoid receptor agonism
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: suppression of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: patients receiving moderately-high to highly emetogenic multi-day chemotherapy
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Complete Response (no emetic episodes and no use of rescue therapy) on cycle 1, day 1

results.effect_size: 84% complete response rate on cycle 1, day 1

dose_info.dose: aprepitant 125 mg (day 1), 80 mg (days 2+); ondansetron 24 mg/day; dexamethasone 12 mg/day (during chemo), 4 mg q12h (post-chemo)
dose_info.schedule: once daily, given 1 hour before chemotherapy; post-chemo dexamethasone q12h x2 days; aprepitant 80 mg daily x2 days post-chemo

modulation_entries.hypothesis: 5-HT3 antagonism by ondansetron blocks the serotonergic pathway of emesis, complementing NK1 antagonism by aprepitant to more completely suppress chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting
modulation_entries.citation: On day 1, the subject will receive a total daily dose of oral dexamethasone 12mg, oral ondansetron 24mg, and oral aprepitant 125mg.

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Dexamethasone's anti-inflammatory effects augment the antiemetic efficacy of aprepitant by reducing central and peripheral inflammatory mediators involved in chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting
